title: pybind11
subtitle: pybind11 binds ActiveKV's C++ engine into vLLM and PyTorch; a line-by-line audit proves every remaining Python line is a framework contract.

lede: In ActiveKV the Python version proved the design and was too slow on the per-token path, and it left the product logic as readable source. I moved the whole runtime to C++ inside vLLM, with pybind11 as the boundary, built against PyTorch's ATen. The port is told in Rewriting an engine extension without changing a token, and how I proved the native code was the code that ran is in Proving a rewrite is the same system. The hard part of a binding layer is deciding what may stay in Python.
quote: The language boundary is a contract I minimise and justify line by line.
evidence: C++ and native ports with parity proof: a Python runtime moved to C++ inside vLLM, 866 of 867 Python dispatch sites made direct native calls, parity cells matched bit for bit.
Python and C++ interoperability with pybind11: 67 binding modules into vLLM and PyTorch, and a line-by-line audit leaving only cited framework contracts in Python.
Release engineering for native extensions: a native launcher that embeds the Python interpreter, and a release of compiled binaries plus a patch with 0 lines of my own Python.
